targetText: They are equal because the constant capital-value re-appearing in II is equal to the value newly produced by I (value of variable capital plus surplus-value); therefore I(v + s) can buy the part of the product of II which represents the constant capital-value for its producers (in department II).
explanation: Department I represents the branch of production that manufactures means of production (machinery, raw materials, industrial equipment).

targetText: They are equal because the constant capital-value re-appearing in II is equal to the value newly produced by I (value of variable capital plus surplus-value); therefore I(v + s) can buy the part of the product of II which represents the constant capital-value for its producers (in department II).
explanation: Department II represents the branch of social production that produces consumer goods and means of individual consumption.

targetText: On the assumption of simple reproduction the total value of the annually produced articles of consumption is therefore equal to the annual value-product, i.
explanation: Social reproduction requires continuous exchange between Department I and Department II to balance industrial equipment needs with consumer wage goods.
